nodes.description: Biallelic inactivating CYP11B2 variants reduce or abolish aldosterone synthase (P450c11AS) activity. Enzymatic activity generally has to fall below about 1% of normal before aldosterone synthesis is impaired; the pattern of residual 11beta-hydroxylase, 18-hydroxylase and 18-oxidase activity determines the CMO I versus CMO II steroid profile.

evidence.reference_title: Aldosterone synthase deficiency and related disorders.
evidence.snippet: Many mutations have been documented in each of these genes; in general enzymatic activity must be reduced to <1% of normal for aldosterone biosynthesis to be impaired.

evidence.reference_title: Five novel mutations in CYP11B2 gene detected in patients with aldosterone synthase deficiency type I: Functional characterization and structural analyses.
evidence.snippet: The expression studies of the mutant proteins in COS-1 cells showed a complete absence of CYP11B2 activity of p.S315R and p.R374W mutants for the conversion of 11-deoxycorticosterone to aldosterone.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Analysis of the CYP11B2 Gene in 62 Patients with Hypoaldosteronism Due to Aldosterone Synthase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Importantly, 96% of the 56 patients carried the previously reported p.T185I variant either in homozygosity or in compound heterozygosity with another variant.

evidence.reference_title: Catch-up Growth and Discontinuation of Fludrocortisone Treatment in Aldosterone Synthase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The most common variant (40%) was p.T185I.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital hyperreninemic hypoaldosteronism in Israel: sequence analysis of CYP11B2 gene.
evidence.snippet: We could not find a molecular defect in 2 patients: one was a carrier of the D335G mutation and the other had no detectable molecular change in the coding and promoter regions.

nodes.description: Volume depletion drives renin secretion; plasma renin activity is markedly elevated in affected infants and young children but may be normal in adults.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Patients with Corticosterone Methyloxidase Deficiency Type 2: Novel Mutations in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: Plasma renin activity is significantly increased in affected infants and young children (up to 100-fold normal) but can be normal in adults.

nodes.description: Aldosterone is low, or inappropriately normal relative to the elevated renin (particularly in CMO II).

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Patients with Corticosterone Methyloxidase Deficiency Type 2: Novel Mutations in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: All patients had normal cortisol response to adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test and had elevated plasma renin activity with low aldosterone levels.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary defect in biosynthesis of aldosterone: aldosterone synthase deficiency 1964-1997.
evidence.snippet: Aldosterone and 18-OH-corticosterone were decreased

nodes.description: Hypovolemic dehydration, sometimes severe, in the first weeks or months of life.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Analysis of the CYP11B2 Gene in 62 Patients with Hypoaldosteronism Due to Aldosterone Synthase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Isolated congenital hypoaldosteronism presents in early infancy with symptoms including vomiting, severe dehydration, salt wasting, and failure to thrive.

nodes.description: Poor weight gain is the most common presenting symptom; growth delay can be the only sign in milder or later-diagnosed cases, and catch-up growth follows treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Catch-up Growth and Discontinuation of Fludrocortisone Treatment in Aldosterone Synthase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: The most common symptom was poor weight gain (56.3%).

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of arginine-173 in the CYP11B2 gene in a girl with congenital hypoaldosteronism. Corticosterone methyloxidase deficiency type II.
evidence.snippet: The first child of consanguineous parents presented with failure to thrive and feeding problems at age 6 weeks.

nodes.description: Oral fludrocortisone replaces mineralocorticoid action, correcting electrolyte disturbances and producing rapid catch-up growth. The dose requirement wanes with age and therapy can be discontinued in many children, but long-term surveillance is advised because the enzymatic defect persists.

evidence.reference_title: Catch-up Growth and Discontinuation of Fludrocortisone Treatment in Aldosterone Synthase Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Fludrocortisone could be stopped in 5 patients at a median age of 6.0 years (range: 2.2 to 7.6).

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of novel heterozygous mutations in the CYP11B2 gene causing congenital aldosterone synthase deficiency and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Fludrocortisone treatment is essential for ASD, and the need for mineralocorticoid replacement wanes with age; eventually, therapy can be discontinued for many affected children.

nodes.description: Elevated serum potassium, typically 6.0-8.5 mmol/L in untreated infants.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Patients with Corticosterone Methyloxidase Deficiency Type 2: Novel Mutations in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: In untreated infants with CMOD, serum sodium level is generally between 120-130 mmol/L and serum potassium level is between 6.0-8.5 mmol/L

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of novel heterozygous mutations in the CYP11B2 gene causing congenital aldosterone synthase deficiency and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Aldosterone synthase deficiency (ASD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by severe hyperkalemia, salt loss, vomiting, severe dehydration and failure to thrive.

nodes.description: Low serum sodium, typically 120-130 mmol/L in untreated infants.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Patients with Corticosterone Methyloxidase Deficiency Type 2: Novel Mutations in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: Biochemical studies showed hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and acidosis.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of arginine-173 in the CYP11B2 gene in a girl with congenital hypoaldosteronism. Corticosterone methyloxidase deficiency type II.
evidence.snippet: Important laboratory findings were low plasma sodium and elevated potassium and renin.

nodes.description: Aldosterone synthase catalyzes the terminal 11beta-hydroxylation, 18-hydroxylation and 18-oxidation steps converting 11-deoxycorticosterone to aldosterone in zona glomerulosa cells. Its loss produces isolated aldosterone deficiency with intact cortisol synthesis, which is CYP11B1-dependent.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the human CYP11B2 (aldosterone synthase) gene causing corticosterone methyloxidase II deficiency.
evidence.snippet: P450XIB2 catalyzes the synthesis of aldosterone from deoxycorticosterone, a process that successively requires hydroxylation at positions 11 beta and 18 and oxidation at position 18.

evidence.reference_title: Neonatal salt wasting syndrome: Aldosterone synthase deficiency caused by a new splicing variant in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: Aldosterone synthase deficiency (ASD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder involving isolated aldosterone deficiency without any compromise of other adrenal hormones.

nodes.description: Markedly elevated plasma renin activity (hyperreninemia), most pronounced in infancy.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Patients with Corticosterone Methyloxidase Deficiency Type 2: Novel Mutations in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: All patients had normal cortisol response to adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test and had elevated plasma renin activity with low aldosterone levels.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Patients with Corticosterone Methyloxidase Deficiency Type 2: Novel Mutations in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: These findings may include vomiting, dehydration, hypovolemia, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis.

nodes.description: Urinary sodium loss caused by absent aldosterone action, presenting as a neonatal salt-wasting syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Neonatal salt wasting syndrome: Aldosterone synthase deficiency caused by a new splicing variant in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: This condition manifests mainly in the neonatal period and in infants as a salt wasting syndrome with vomiting and failure to thrive.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of arginine-173 in the CYP11B2 gene in a girl with congenital hypoaldosteronism. Corticosterone methyloxidase deficiency type II.
evidence.snippet: Salt wasting was caused by an enzymatic defect in the terminal aldosterone biosynthesis.

nodes.description: Without aldosterone, distal nephron and collecting duct principal cells fail to reabsorb sodium and secrete potassium, producing urinary sodium loss, hypovolemia, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and metabolic acidosis.
nodes.id: Renal sodium wasting and potassium retention

evidence.reference_title: Aldosterone synthase deficiency and related disorders.
evidence.snippet: Aldosterone's main actions are to regulate intravascular volume and serum electrolytes by controlling sodium absorbtion and potassium excretion in the distal nephron.

nodes.description: Oral salt supplementation, together with rehydration in acute presentations, is used alongside fludrocortisone, particularly in infancy.

evidence.reference_title: Neonatal salt wasting syndrome: Aldosterone synthase deficiency caused by a new splicing variant in CYP11B2.
evidence.snippet: rehydration as well as salt and fludrocortisone supplementation
